subject.title: feat(feeds): search and follow signed publisher feeds

question: Should OpenClaw core own a durable signed publisher-feed consumer and `openclaw publisher` lifecycle, or should publisher discovery/following remain a ClawHub/plugin capability until a missing generic core extension API is identified?
rationale: The PR adds a new core product and trust boundary rather than repairing an established behavior, while repository direction explicitly prefers optional capabilities and publisher concerns outside core when existing extension seams suffice.

options.title: Keep the capability out of core
options.body: Route publisher discovery and following to a ClawHub/plugin package unless the contributor can demonstrate a missing generic core API.

options.title: Sponsor a generic core primitive
options.body: Approve only narrowly reusable signed-feed primitives in core, with publisher-specific commands and policy owned by ClawHub or a plugin.

options.title: Accept the full core workflow
options.body: Approve the core CLI and SQLite lifecycle as a strategic OpenClaw feature, then require live producer-to-consumer proof and an explicit compatibility contract.

recommendation.title: Keep the capability out of core
recommendation.body: Route publisher discovery and following to a ClawHub/plugin package unless the contributor can demonstrate a missing generic core API.

likelyOwner.reason: Best available routing candidate for the repository-level core-versus-plugin product boundary.
